sources.author: Alex Kanaris-Sotiriou
sources.used: Read article text and viewed KeyPoses_Wide.jpg and Roll_Pitch_Yaw.jpg; no video viewed.
sources.principles: Alternating contacts and passing positions; opposed arms; hips participate in the transfer of support. Character proportions and weight determine the result.
sources.adaptation: Use the existing boy profile and preserve its flat painted construction. In-plane pelvic pitch/translation stands in for the weight transfer idea; no literal 3D hip yaw or head turnaround.

sources.used: Read article text and inspected eight static samples from its 56-frame Tove_Walk_Breakdown.gif illustration. This is illustrated reference study, not normal-speed video observation.
sources.principles: New support compresses under load; head/chest can respond after the hips; lower arm overlap can soften simultaneous motion. Amounts depend on the character.
sources.adaptation: Small source-proportion compression/rebound; one-frame chest phase offset, two-frame head offset and 1.5-frame lower-arm phase offset. The existing head view stays unchanged.

sources.used: Earlier parent handoff supplied the documented two-bone/pole/optional-stretch principles. Direct fetch here returned402, so this is not claimed as independently retrieved documentation. Actual bpy chain settings and lengths were inspected and tested.

limits: No new quarter-view art; boy-only capability exercise. Child rig has unequal drawn limb reach; hip path is deliberately asymmetric inside both native envelopes. No leg stretch. Deep cloth and folded/crossing-arm defects remain failure criteria, not inferred passes.
